issues.description: The successful write-to-upgradeable downgrade returns the new guard without waking waiters that were blocked by the old write lock.
issues.rationale: The successful compare_exchange(WRITER, UPGRADEABLE_READER) already replaces the WRITER bit with the upgradeable-reader bit: these are distinct bits at positions usize::BITS-1 and usize::BITS-2. Therefore this path does not retain a stale WRITER bit. The concrete regression is the missing wake-up: the original success path called drop(self), whose release path wakes the queue, while the selected try_downgrade immediately returns the upgradeable guard after CAS and never calls queue.wake_all(). Waiting readers that could now proceed are not notified by this downgrade. The explicit write-guard drop helper still contains wake_all at line 789. This narrows the historical missing-drop report to the executable side effect supported by the fixed source; no runtime concurrency test was executed.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus and runtime tests not executed. Compared the fixed 6ae195e508a8 snapshot, complete archived/current remote review history, the original drop implementation, dedicated fix commits, and final approved head fc59447fa7c2119c3e0cdd132f2cb2e8d85c00fc.
